top_stories.title: Musk v. Altman Is a Battle for OpenAI's Soul
top_stories.summary: Wired reports on the legal and philosophical clash between Elon Musk and Sam Altman, framing the lawsuit as a fight over the fundamental direction and control of OpenAI. The case touches on OpenAI's transition from a nonprofit to a for-profit entity and what that means for its original mission. The outcome could have significant implications for AI governance and the future structure of one of the world's most influential AI companies.

top_stories.title: OpenAI's big Codex update is a direct shot at Claude Code [Paywalled]
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has released a major update to Codex, its AI coding tool, positioning it as a direct competitor to Anthropic's Claude Code. The update includes new capabilities for use on macOS and expands Codex's functionality for software development workflows. The move signals an intensifying rivalry in the AI coding assistant space.

top_stories.title: Google's AI Mode Update Tries to Kill Tab Hopping in Chrome
top_stories.summary: Google has updated its AI Mode to allow users to open source links without leaving the current page, reducing the need to switch between browser tabs. The feature is designed to make AI-assisted search more seamless and keep users within the AI Mode interface. The update represents Google's continued effort to integrate generative AI more deeply into its core search product.

top_stories.title: The UK Launches Its $675 Million Sovereign AI Fund
top_stories.summary: The UK government has announced a $675 million sovereign AI fund aimed at building domestic AI capabilities and reducing reliance on foreign technology providers. The initiative is part of the country's broader strategy to position itself as a leading AI nation. The fund is expected to support AI infrastructure, research, and homegrown AI development.

top_stories.title: The 'AI is inevitable' trap [Paywalled]
top_stories.summary: The Vergecast examines the rhetoric around AI inevitability, questioning whether framing AI adoption as unavoidable serves the interests of technology companies more than the public. The discussion draws on Sam Altman's public statements and broader industry messaging. The episode raises questions about technological determinism and the choices still available to societies around AI.

further_links.title: AI warfare's human illusion — MIT Technology Review
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines the concept of 'human in the loop' in AI-enabled warfare, questioning whether human oversight in autonomous weapons systems is as meaningful as claimed.

further_links.title: How robots learn: A brief, contemporary history — MIT Technology Review
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review traces the recent evolution of robot learning, covering advances in machine learning techniques that have transformed how robots acquire and generalise skills.

further_links.title: Microsoft Expands Copilot and AI Agent Capabilities in Power Apps
further_links.summary: Microsoft has announced expanded Copilot and AI agent features within its Power Apps platform, enabling more automation and natural language interaction for business application development.

further_links.title: xAI rolls out Grok 4.3 beta for SuperGrok Heavy subscribers
further_links.summary: xAI has released a beta version of Grok 4.3, making it available to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers as the company continues iterating on its large language model.

further_links.title: Forbes 2026 AI 50 List | Top Artificial Intelligence Companies
further_links.summary: Forbes has published its 2026 AI 50 list, highlighting the most promising private artificial intelligence companies across industries.

further_links.title: CIOs Struggle to Deliver Business Value as AI and Complexity Expose Gaps in Their Applications Strategy
further_links.summary: A new Info-Tech Research Group report finds that CIOs are finding it difficult to translate AI investments into measurable business value, with application complexity emerging as a key barrier.

further_links.title: The beginning of scarcity in AI — Tom Tunguz
further_links.summary: Venture capitalist Tom Tunguz argues that AI compute is entering a period of genuine scarcity in 2026, with demand for inference and training capacity outpacing available supply and reshaping competitive dynamics.

further_links.title: George Orwell Predicted the Rise of 'AI Slop' in Nineteen Eighty-Four
further_links.summary: Open Culture draws parallels between Orwell's concept of machine-generated propaganda in Nineteen Eighty-Four and the modern phenomenon of low-quality, algorithmically produced AI content.

further_links.title: Google's AI Mode update lets you open links without leaving the page [Paywalled]
further_links.summary: Google's latest AI Mode update introduces an in-page link-opening feature, allowing users to browse sources cited by AI search results without navigating away.
